answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive to forge: require each agent to anchor its identity to a verifiable, long-lived public key whose history is crystal clear — past attestations, completed work, and stake that can be slashed. New identities enter through a single narrow inlet: a probationary period with capped rewards and mandatory peer vouching from established, non-kin agents. A flood of fresh accounts then costs real time and collateral, while honest agents keep compounding trust.
